title.narrative: Socio-cultural attitudes and practices, accountability, and legal and policy frameworks are transformed to eliminate gender-based violence and all forms of abuse, exploitation and discrimination against vulnerable groups

description.narrative: Viet Nam is committed to eradicating child labor, with a specific focus on its worst forms, ensuring children's rights to a safe childhood, education, and development. This commitment reflects the government's recognition of every child's fundamental right to a nurturing, labor-free childhood. The ILO supports Vietnam's tripartite partners in achieving these goals through robust capacity-building initiatives, empowering national institutions and stakeholders with the tools and knowledge needed to combat child labor effectively. Enhanced monitoring and response mechanisms enable timely identification and intervention in exploitation cases, complemented by targeted awareness campaigns. While children engaged in or at risk of hazardous labor and their families are the primary beneficiaries, ILO's support also yields significant benefits for employers, government agencies, trade unions, community organizations, and civil society groups. These efforts collectively contribute to a sustainable, child-labor-free environment across Vietnamese society.
